content:
# Firstmate integration scripts

The command-line contract Wheelhouse consumes from a Firstmate checkout's
`bin/`: `fm-fleet-snapshot.sh --json` (fleet and task state),
`fm-inbox.sh ready` (supervisor readiness), `fm-inbox.sh note --request-id
<id> --json -` (send a message; the only write), `fm-inbox.sh receipts
[--after <cursor>]` (acks and replies) and `fm-peek.sh <task> <lines>` (worker
terminal output, at most 200 lines). Outputs are versioned JSON schemas;
Wheelhouse checks marker strings in each script at startup and reports
incompatibility in `/api/health` rather than refusing to start.

Owned by Firstmate, not this repository; known here only from Wheelhouse's
side of the contract.
title: Firstmate integration scripts

content:
# Wheelhouse HTTP API

The loopback-only JSON API the Wheelhouse pages use (routes under
`src/routes/api/`): `GET /api/health`, `/api/fleet`, `/api/tasks/:id`,
`/api/tasks/:id/output`, `/api/tasks/:id/artifacts/...`, `GET`/`POST
/api/firstmate/messages` (POST takes an `Idempotency-Key`), `/api/events`
(server-sent events: `fleet`, `health`, `messages`), `/api/plugins` and
`/api/slots`. Specs: `POST /api/specs` (create), `GET /api/specs/:id`
(retrieve draft), `PUT /api/specs/:id` (update), `GET
/api/specs/:id/images/:name` (serve uploaded images), `POST
/api/specs/:id/sent` (mark sent—sets sentAt only, does not overwrite
edits). Mutating requests are guarded as described in
[[constraint.loopback-only-with-origin-token]]. Not versioned.
title: Wheelhouse HTTP API

content:
# External commands run as bounded argument arrays, never via a shell

Firstmate scripts, `git` and `gh` run through `runBounded`
(`src/lib/server/firstmate/exec.ts`): argument arrays, timeouts, output caps,
their own process group, and closed stdin except the message body written to
`fm-inbox.sh note` (at most 16 KiB). Plugin `exec` goes through the same runner
with a minimal environment.
title: External commands run as bounded argument arrays, never via a shell

content:
# Command check consent language must be honest about scope

The UI and documentation for consenting to command checks must clearly state
that consent covers the command line itself, not the scripts or behavior
those commands invoke at runtime.

## Rationale

The original wording implied that any change to what a command runs turns
consent off again. This is not accurate. If the command line (argv) stays
constant but the scripts it calls change (through a merged PR), the command
runs under the earlier consent. This is an important distinction that users
must understand to make informed consent decisions.

## Implementation

- Update the passage page's command consent section to state plainly:
  "Allowing command checks trusts the project's own scripts at the commit
  they run on. Consent covers the command line, not the scripts it calls,
  which can change through merged pull requests."

- Update the check form's "Exactly what will run" panel with similar
  transparent language.

- Update `docs/passages.md` to reflect this reality.

- Retain the statement that changing a command line turns consent off again.

- Remove wording that misleads users about what changes require new consent.

## Impact

This constraint ensures users understand the trust model for command checks
and can make informed security decisions about what scripts they authorize
to run.
title: Command check consent language must be honest about scope

content:
# Command checks run in temporary worktrees at pinned commits

Command checks for passage stages must execute in isolated, temporary git
worktrees checked out at a specific, deterministic commit, never in the
Firstmate project clone's working tree.

## Rationale

The Firstmate project clone's working tree may contain stale, unrelated, or
uncommitted code. If command checks run there, a task's 'Deployed' or other
passages can pass after deploying code that is not the task's merge commit,
and scripts that change through merged PRs can run under earlier consent.

## Implementation

- Create a temporary worktree from the project clone, checked out (detached)
  at the pinned commit: the task's merge commit for `ref: merge.commit`,
  the pull request head for `ref: pr.head`, or the default-branch tip
  (`clone.defaultRef`, e.g. `origin/main`) otherwise.

- Resolve the working directory inside that worktree with the same path
  boundary enforcement (paths that escape the worktree are rejected).

- Pass `WHEELHOUSE_COMMIT` as the commit actually checked out, and verify
  it matches.

- Worktree path must be deterministic per run (e.g., under Wheelhouse's
  state directory or the OS temp directory, named from task id, check id,
  and commit).

- Remove the worktree afterwards with `git worktree remove --force <exact path>`
  (no `rm` with globs or variables), including when the command fails, times out,
  or the commit cannot be checked out.

- Test dry-runs (`service.dryRun`) must use the same pinned checkout.

- If the commit cannot be checked out, the check reports that outcome with
  an explanation.

## Testing

- Command runs in a worktree at the pinned commit, not in the clone's
  working tree (which has different content).
- The worktree is removed afterwards, including after a failure.
- `WHEELHOUSE_COMMIT` matches the commit checked out.
title: Command checks run in temporary worktrees at pinned commits

content:
# Loopback only; mutations need same Origin and session token

Wheelhouse listens on `127.0.0.1` only and answers only `Host` values
`127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `[::1]` (anything else gets 421, blocking DNS
rebinding). Every mutating request must carry an `Origin` equal to the served
`http://<host>` and echo the per-launch session token (header
`x-wheelhouse-session`), which is random per process and never written to disk;
otherwise 403.
title: Loopback only; mutations need same Origin and session token

content:
# Read-only toward Firstmate; all messages go to Firstmate

Wheelhouse attaches without changing Firstmate's configuration and never
starts, stops or controls Firstmate or its workers. Its only write is
`fm-inbox.sh note`; every message goes to Firstmate, never directly to a
worker; worker output is inspectable but cannot accept input; and closing
Wheelhouse must not interrupt work. Plugins inherit the same limit.
title: Read-only toward Firstmate; all messages go to Firstmate

content:
# Specs limited to 16 KiB when sent to Firstmate

Spec drafts cannot exceed 16 KiB (16384 bytes) when sent to Firstmate. The
Send button in the Spec tab is disabled with a plain message if the serialized
spec exceeds this limit. A POST to `/api/specs/:id/sent` returns HTTP 413
(Payload Too Large) if the spec is too large. The constraint comes from
Firstmate's inbox message size limit when Firstmate is running as a separate
service (not co-located).
title: Specs limited to 16 KiB when sent to Firstmate

content:
# Test panel command consent tied to displayed command digest

The test panel's "Also run these commands" checkbox must enforce that
the commands actually run match the exact list displayed when the captain
ticked the box.

## Problem

The test panel's `runCommands` checkbox stays ticked when the file's commands
change. The list of commands displayed comes from the debounced draft (300 ms
plus a network round trip). The server's `dryRun` endpoint runs every command
in the submitted text whenever `runCommands === true`, without verifying they
match what was displayed.

**Race condition**: The captain ticks the box while seeing command list A,
then edits A into B in the YAML editor and clicks "Run the test" before
the draft refreshes. B runs on the captain's machine, though the displayed
list showed A.

Even after the list refreshes, the old tick carries over to the new commands,
creating consent confusion.

## Implementation

- Send the digest of the commands listed (`commandsDigest` of the draft's
  commands at the time of test submission) with the test request.

- The server's `dryRun` endpoint (service.ts:705) must refuse with a 409
  status code when the submitted digest differs from the actual commands in
  the text, returning a clear message asking the captain to review again.

- Reset the `runCommands` state whenever the listed commands change, so the
  tick does not automatically carry to newly displayed commands.

## Testing

- Verify that ticking the checkbox with command list A and then editing
  to list B before submission causes the server to reject with 409.

- Verify that changing the commands resets the `runCommands` checkbox.

## Related

This constraint mirrors the behavior of the `commands-consent` endpoint
(which the captain must explicitly approve before running any commands),
ensuring test command execution requires deliberate, informed consent.
title: Test panel command consent tied to displayed command digest

content:
# Firstmate operational home

Firstmate's state directory tree, read directly (never written) by Wheelhouse:
`state/fleet-ledger.jsonl` (tailed, when the ledger is on), `data/projects.md`
(project descriptions), and per task `data/<id>/contributions.json`,
`data/<id>/report.md` and screenshots. Task diffs come from `git diff` in the
worktree Firstmate recorded. Located by `--home`, else `$FM_HOME`, else the
Firstmate checkout.
title: Firstmate operational home

content:
# Wheelhouse state directory (message store)

Wheelhouse's only persistent state: a `wheelhouse-message-store.v1` JSON file
per Firstmate home holding sent messages, delivery outcomes, receipts and the
receipts cursor (at most 500 messages). Directory: `--state-dir`, else
`$WHEELHOUSE_STATE_DIR`, else `$XDG_STATE_HOME/wheelhouse`, else
`~/.local/state/wheelhouse`; it must be outside the Firstmate home. Plugin
enablement lives separately in `plugins.json` in the config directory.
title: Wheelhouse state directory (message store)

content:
# Plugins are compiled in, filling fixed slots

Plugins are "panels and providers": first-party code compiled into Wheelhouse
and registered in `BUILTIN_PLUGINS`. There are no microfrontends, iframes or
runtime-loaded bundles, and plugins cannot add slots - they contribute to five
fixed slots using versioned blocks or their own Svelte panel. Read-only is the
plugin's contract, reviewed in Wheelhouse's pull requests, not a sandbox.
title: Plugins are compiled in, filling fixed slots

content:
# Docket Chart design decisions

## Approved design principles

The docket Chart visualization uses nautical metaphor for system topology:
- **Regions by owner**: Components grouped by team/organization ownership
- **Production as harbour**: Special visual treatment for production environments
- **Constraints as restricted waters**: Dashed/dotted lines for durable constraints
- **Vessels overlay**: In-flight tasks shown as vessels on the system map they touch
- **Evidence confidence styling**: Line styles indicate relationship confidence level

Clean, easy-to-understand presentation without internal technical jargon.

## Integration decisions

### Docket binary configuration
**Decision**: Docket binary is a plugin setting with PATH as default.

**Rationale**: Allows projects to use custom docket versions while defaulting to system PATH, 
fitting Wheelhouse's plugin architecture.

**Implementation**: Plugin loads docket from settings or PATH, displays error state if version
is too old (e.g., doesn't support `graph --json`).

### Fixture data approach
**Decision**: No runtime fallback to bundled fixtures; keep opt-in only.

**Rationale**: Fixture data (docket's examples/acme-platform) is used only when explicitly
configured. This avoids surprising behavior and keeps fixture-based exploration intentional.

**Implementation**: Smoke tests remain disabled for wheelhouse (no auto-enabling of Chart
without docket). Documentation clearly describes `settings.roots` + `projects` config required
to enable Chart for a project.

### Docket CLI error handling
**Decision**: Show "docket CLI too old for the Chart - update docket" when `graph --json` is unsupported.

**Rationale**: Clear, actionable feedback when docket version doesn't support required features.

**Implementation**: readGraph provider catches unsupported command and renders friendly error state
in Chart card rather than silent failure.

### Open in docket linkout
**Decision**: Show copyable `docket open --root <path>` command next to the "Open in docket" link.

**Rationale**: Users unfamiliar with docket CLI get direct, copy-paste-ready command instead of
relying on dead link when docket viewer isn't running or uses different port.

**Implementation**: Chart component displays both the link (for convenience if viewer is running)
and the CLI command (for reliability and discoverability).

## Out-of-scope decisions

### Not editable in Wheelhouse
Chart is intentionally read-only. Editing system maps happens in docket itself, not in Wheelhouse.
Reduces surface area and keeps editing in the domain-specific tool where all docket features are available.

### No Ask/Chat in Chart
Wheelhouse design keeps Chart and other plugins chat-free. Users open docket directly for discussion.
title: Docket Chart design for Wheelhouse system map

content:
# Trim Docket Chart UI

## Decision

Remove the "Waters this passage crosses" panel from task pages and the "Hazards ahead" 
card from Harbour. Both features are display-only and do not inform the build process.

Enhance the Chart itself to display full-width with the detail inspector positioned
on the right side, similar to the Firstmate chat layout, making better use of screen 
real estate and improving readability.

## Rationale

- **Waters section**: Appears on task pages after the Building step; purely informational, 
  shows which system components a task touches but does not drive build decisions
- **Hazards card**: Appears on Harbour only when in-flight tasks touch constrained exhibits; 
  alerts teams but does not provide actionable guidance during the build
- **Value assessment**: Both panels add visual complexity without providing build-time value
- **Performance**: Removing them simplifies the Harbour and task page interfaces

## Removed 2026-10-25

- Waters section from task pages (display-only informational)
- Hazards card from Harbour (display-only alerting)

## Changes

- Chart enhanced to full-width layout with inspector details pane on right
- Chart made more prominent and easier to read
- Legacy `/harbour?tab=...` tab redirect removed
title: Trim Docket Chart UI - remove display-only panels

content:
# Pin SvelteKit 2 rather than SvelteKit 3

Wheelhouse uses SvelteKit 2 with Svelte 5, Vite 7, Tailwind 4 and
shadcn-svelte. The UI prototype ran on SvelteKit 3 but needed workarounds for
shadcn-svelte (`#lib` aliases, a crash on `extends: "$app/tsconfig"`, patched
component state attributes). SvelteKit 2 works with standard `$lib` aliases and
generated components, so this build pins it. Moving to SvelteKit 3 is a later,
separate change once shadcn-svelte supports it cleanly.
title: Pin SvelteKit 2 rather than SvelteKit 3

content:
# Messages carry a stable request id for idempotent delivery

Every message gets a request id in the browser, sent as `Idempotency-Key` and
recorded by Wheelhouse before it runs `fm-inbox.sh note --request-id <id>`.
Retries, double clicks and reconciliation reuse it; Firstmate returns the
original note for a repeated id, so no duplicate is ever created. Delivery and
acknowledgement are tracked as separate states.
title: Messages carry a stable request id for idempotent delivery

content:
# Put all text on solid white/card backgrounds in Wheelhouse UI

## Decision

All text in the Wheelhouse UI (page headings, intros, empty states, lists, chat, insights, Spec tab, passage editor, task page's Docs tab, and other content surfaces) should sit on solid white or card backgrounds instead of directly on the graph-paper grid.

## Context

Wheelhouse's design draws a faint 48px graph-paper grid on the main background. Side panels are solid surfaces, but several text areas previously sat directly on the grid, making text hard to read and reducing contrast.

## Why

Text legibility and visual hierarchy. The grid provides aesthetic continuity but is not a good surface for reading text. Solid backgrounds significantly improve readability and provide a distinct, professional presentation of content.

## Consequences

- Text in all views (page headings, docs, task details, chat, specs, passages, live consoles) now sits on white or card backgrounds
- The grid background remains visible behind non-text UI elements
- Docs tab now renders markdown as a proper document view (not inline)
- Live consoles are clickable to open full-screen (separate improvement validated alongside this one)

## Confirmation

User tested and confirmed (2026-10-26): "text on white looks good". All scenarios in the test phase passed.
title: Put all text on solid white/card backgrounds in Wheelhouse UI

# Bridge focused on one thread at a time

The Bridge UI now focuses on viewing a single thread at a time rather than
showing all Wheelhouse messages, Firstmate replies, and reports in one long
stream. This addresses the user intent to reduce clutter and help the captain
see only what they are responding to.

When viewing a decision (a captain-held backlog task with a question and
options), the Bridge now shows the decision's question and options inline
rather than only as a card linking back to the overview.

The feature is validated by a smoke test that checks the Bridge serves the
focused task thread correctly.

Displays the worker's review questions and Firstmate's decisions on the Harbour

content:
# Command checks for passage stages

Command checks allow projects to run shell commands to verify passage stage
completion. Useful for custom integrations like local Kubernetes deployments,
status APIs, or project-specific build artifacts.

## Mechanism

- Defined as `run:` in `.wheelhouse.yaml` passage stage rules
- Command runs in a temporary, isolated worktree at the pinned commit
- Can be tested interactively in the passage editor's test panel
- Requires captain consent (both on the project configuration panel and when
  testing)

## Example: Local deployment

```yaml
# .wheelhouse.yaml
stages:
  - name: Deployed locally
    reached_when: 
      check: local.deploy
      expected: ok
    
checks:
  local.deploy:
    run: [pnpm, deploy:local]
    timeout: 300000  # 5 minutes
```

Runs `pnpm deploy:local` to verify a local Kubernetes deployment succeeded.

## Constraints

- Runs in a temporary worktree at the pinned commit, never in the clone's
  working tree (security, reproducibility): [[constraint.command-checks-pinned-worktree]]
- Consent language is transparent about what it covers: [[constraint.command-checks-consent-language]]
- Test panel consent tied to displayed command digest: [[constraint.test-consent-digest-binding]]
title: Command checks for passage stages

content:
# Fleet collector (polling and SSE)

The single shared collector (`src/lib/server/collector/collector.ts`). Every
~5 s it reads Firstmate readiness and new fleet-ledger lines; the full fleet
snapshot runs on an adaptive cadence between 5 and 30 s. Results are cached in
memory and pushed to the browser over server-sent events (`/api/events`). A
failed read keeps the last good view but marks it stale. Each round also
reconciles messages sent to Firstmate.

Modelled as a `library` (internal module); see [[library.firstmate-adapter]].
title: Fleet collector (polling and SSE)

content:
# Commander

Argument parsing for the `wheelhouse` CLI (`cli/index.ts`, bundled by esbuild
into `dist/cli.js`). It is the package's only runtime `dependency`; everything
else is a devDependency bundled at build time.
title: Commander

content:
# Firstmate script adapter

Everything under `src/lib/server/firstmate/`: `install.ts` resolves the
Firstmate checkout and home and checks each script's contract markers;
`exec.ts` (`runBounded`) runs commands as argument arrays with timeouts and
output caps; `adapter.ts` wraps `fm-fleet-snapshot.sh`, `fm-inbox.sh`
(ready/note/receipts) and `fm-peek.sh`; `contracts.ts` parses their versioned
JSON; `ledger.ts` tails the fleet ledger; `evidence.ts` assembles per-task
evidence (diffs, PR state, report, screenshots, CI readiness); `stages.ts` and
`model.ts` derive the passage stages shown in the UI.

Modelled as a `library` because the default ontology has no internal-module
type; it is not published separately.
title: Firstmate script adapter

content:
# Message store and messenger

`src/lib/server/store/`: `store.ts` persists Wheelhouse's own record of
messages it sent (request id, body, delivery outcome, receipts, cursor) under
the Wheelhouse state directory, never inside the Firstmate home, writing via a
temp file renamed over the old one. `messenger.ts` sends through `fm-inbox.sh
note` with a stable request id and re-issues uncertain or unannounced sends on
a 15 s-to-5 min backoff.

Modelled as a `library` (internal module).
title: Message store and messenger

content:
# Plugin slots, registry and blocks

Compiled-in "panels and providers" (`src/lib/plugins/` for the slot and
block contract and panels, `src/lib/server/plugins/` for the registry and
`plugins.json` enablement). Five fixed slots (`project.tab`, `harbour.card`,
`task.section`, `step.evidence`, `bridge.card`); versioned blocks (`text.v1` ...
`graph.v1`); contract `apiVersion` 1. Providers run with a timeout and TTL cache
and read only through a confined `readFile` and bounded `exec`. One plugin ships:
`project-links` (`BUILTIN_PLUGINS` in `src/lib/server/plugins/builtin.ts`), off
unless enabled in `plugins.json`.

Modelled as a `library` (internal module).
title: Plugin slots, registry and blocks

content:
# Configurable passage stages (Wheelhouse)

The first feature in Wheelhouse's extensibility roadmap: making passage stages
configurable so projects can define custom stages like Deployed and Released
beyond the built-in ship and scout passages.

## Design

Passages are expressed as data in two parts:
- **Checks**: typed, built-in probes that gather observations (github.deployment,
  github.workflow, github.release, npm.published, http GET/HEAD, git.contains,
  status.note)
- **Stages**: rules over check observations defining when stages are reached and
  what evidence they show

Each project's passage is the built-in ship or scout passage plus a small YAML
file (`.wheelhouse.yaml`) that adds or overrides stages. The built-in passages
are themselves expressible in the same format, so every project works with no
configuration.

## Configuration

**Location and scope**: `.wheelhouse.yaml` at the project's root, read only from
the project's default branch of Firstmate's project clone, never from task
branches or worktrees (prevents crewmates from marking their own passages
Deployed). Layered over built-in passages and under captain-owned Wheelhouse
config overrides (e.g. `~/.config/wheelhouse/`).

**Validation**: Project files require explicit captain approval on a project
panel that lists every check that will run. Wheelhouse records the file's digest
and re-asks if the file changes. Invalid files show a warning and fall back to
built-in passages without blanking the dashboard.

**Schema**: Small and type-safe. Conditions are references (Firstmate facts or
`check.outcome`) combined with `all/any/not` plus mode and yolo predicates; no
expression language, no templating. Unknown types, fields and references are
errors. Values such as merge commits are validated and placed by Wheelhouse code,
never substituted into user strings.

## Stage semantics

- `reached_when`: high-water mark (furthest step whose condition holds is
  current; earlier steps count as done even after task cleanup); terminal
  outcomes are cached
- `skip_when`: mode/yolo-aware conditional skipping
- `failed_when`: makes a later failed step current and shown as failed without
  creating a "Needs you" item
- `give_up_after`: stops polling and reports give-up
- A check that errors is unknown and never silently treated as not reached
- `evidence`: lists what each step shows
- `primary_link`: makes a check's URL the card's primary action
- `headline.live`: names the step that counts toward the watch report's "N live"
  (returns only where declared)

## Polling

Checks run on their interval (minimum 30s) in a background scheduler, only while
the task could still advance, and terminal outcomes are cached. Checks never run
on the fleet's hot path.

## Status

PR #9 on chrisjowen/wheelhouse (branch fm/wh-passages) resolves merge conflicts
and advances toward merge. Implementation covers the core check types and stage
rules.

Command checks are being added in the fm/wh-passage-editor branch (commits
b24e464→923c61f), with architectural decisions documented in review phase:
- Command checks run in temporary worktrees at pinned commits for isolation
  and security
- Consent language updated to be transparent about what consent covers
- Test panel consent tied to displayed command digest to prevent race conditions

Plugins/slots and docket integration remain separate future PRs.
title: Configurable passage stages (Wheelhouse)

content:
# Wheelhouse repository

The source repository for Wheelhouse, a local web UI and CLI companion to
Firstmate (`chrisjowen/wheelhouse`, default branch `main`). It holds one
deliverable - the `wheelhouse` service (SvelteKit app plus Commander CLI) - its
internal server modules, unit and smoke test suites, and the MVP spec under
`docs/spec.md`. The package is private and not published to npm; README says to
install from a clone with `npm ci && npm run build && npm link`.

No CI workflow is checked in (there is no `.github/` directory at this commit).
title: Wheelhouse repository

content:
# Harbour screenshot thumbnails must have constrained size

Requirement from the captain: screenshot evidence thumbnails in the Harbour design should be
displayed at a fixed, constrained size rather than expanding based on image dimensions or viewport.

Applies to:
- Harbour cards (fleet overview page)
- Task page screenshot evidence display

Stated during code-review of task page redesign changes on branch fm/wh-task-layout-left.
title: Harbour screenshot thumbnails must have constrained size

content:
# Task page live terminal and time in left column

Requirement from the captain: the live terminal view and time information (elapsed / where time went)
should be displayed in the left column of the task page alongside the task overview, not in
right-hand tabs.

Stated during code-review of branch fm/wh-task-layout-left, which implements this requirement by
moving the live terminal output and time metrics from behind tab controls on the right to the

title: Task page live terminal and time in left column

content:
# Wheelhouse (local web UI and CLI)

The one runnable thing in the repository: a SvelteKit 2 app built with
adapter-node and launched by a Commander CLI (`wheelhouse open`, the default
command). It attaches to a Firstmate session that is already running, binds
`127.0.0.1` (default port 4310), and opens the browser. Pages: Harbour (fleet
overview), task pages with evidence, and the Bridge (messaging Firstmate).

It reads Firstmate only through its integration scripts and its operational
home, keeps its own message record in a Wheelhouse state directory, and
optionally reads GitHub (via `gh`) and no-mistakes run logs for PR/CI evidence.
Closing it leaves Firstmate and its crew running.

Lifecycle is recorded as `experimental`: version 0.1.0, private package, and the
README says this release covers only the "watch the crew" and "talk to
Firstmate" slices of the MVP. It runs on the operator's machine; there is no
deployed environment.
title: Wheelhouse (local web UI and CLI)

content:
# Firstmate

The agent-fleet orchestrator Wheelhouse watches and talks to
(<https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate>). Wheelhouse needs a Firstmate
checkout (for its `bin/fm-*` scripts) and its operational home (`state/`,
`data/`), resolved from `--firstmate`/`--home`, `$FM_HOME`, or the checkout it
is run inside. Wheelhouse never starts, stops or reconfigures Firstmate.
title: Firstmate

content:
# GitHub (via gh CLI)

Read only as a fallback: when Firstmate has no cached PR observation
(`data/<id>/contributions.json`), Wheelhouse runs `gh pr view <url> --json ...`
with prompts disabled and a 10 s timeout. Optional - without `gh` the PR
evidence says it is unavailable. The `project-links` plugin also builds GitHub
links from repository metadata, without calling GitHub.
title: GitHub (via gh CLI)

content:
# no-mistakes

The validation pipeline Firstmate's workers can ship through. Wheelhouse reads
its local files only: screenshots from `~/.no-mistakes/evidence/<run>/` and the
latest checks marker in `~/.no-mistakes/logs/<run>/ci.log`, to tell when a PR's
CI is green while the monitor is still running. No network or daemon calls are
made from Wheelhouse.
title: no-mistakes

content:
# Smoke tests

Vitest project `smoke` (`npm run test:smoke`, which builds first): starts the
built CLI and server against a fake Firstmate home from
`tests/helpers/fake-firstmate.ts`, with 60 s timeouts.
title: Smoke tests

content:
# Unit tests

Vitest project `unit` (`npm run test:unit`): colocated `*.test.ts` files under
`src/` and `cli/`, covering the adapter, store, messenger, security hooks,
collector and plugins.
title: Unit tests
